texts: doha about how sharing what you have makes it grow
the more you give
Open your hand and abundance returns to you, for what is shared multiplies and what is hoarded decays.
I started sending half my bonus to a village school last year, and somehow my savings feel fuller than ever; I'd like a doha for that strange fact.
Please write a doha about the generous soul who gives freely to anyone in need, without counting, and who discovers that his own store never runs low, but grows in proportion to what he shares.
The palace gate stays closed to the hungry, while the furnace of a poor man's kitchen feeds a stranger; which of the two grows richer?
palace, furnace, generous
The king's palace wastes food every night, but the neighbour with the small furnace in her yard bakes bread for the whole lane, and her family never goes short.
doha with a palace and a furnace, about how sharing makes you richer
Write a doha where a palace hoards its grain behind high walls while a poor woman's furnace warms bread for any hungry passerby, and it is her little that grows into plenty because she shares it.
give and grow
My grandmother never turned a hungry person away from our gate, and in all her years her kitchen never ran short; I want a doha for her.
write a doha about how generosity brings more back to you
Please compose a doha for a person who has just realised that every time he helps someone in need, his own life seems to be filled with more than he gave, so that sharing becomes the surest increase.
The hand that gives is never empty, for the giver is filled by the giving.
A lion shares its kill with the cubs and does not hoard it, and a rope drawn from the village pump brings water for everyone; please write a doha about the way generosity grows by use.
lion, rope, generous
doha with a lion and a rope, about how sharing makes things grow
The rope that draws for all is never worn by use, and the lion that shares its feast is never lonely.
At the village pump, the rope has been used by hundreds of hands, and the old man who keeps it says the more it is shared, the stronger it becomes, and I'd like a doha on that.
ash, shroud, generosity
doha with ash and a shroud, about sharing what you have while you can
Ash and a shroud are all that go with us, so give today, for gifts are the only wealth that outlives the body.
Write a doha where a man in a shroud, his body soon to be ash, regrets all he did not share, and the one who gave freely in life goes with a lighter heart and a fuller name.
My uncle gave away half his land before he died, and at his funeral everyone spoke of him with such love; I'd like a doha about it.
doha about how giving to the poor never makes you poorer
charity multiplies
Scatter your gifts on the roadside, and a thousand blessings will come to you.
Please write a doha about the paradox that a person who gives away much of what he has receives more in peace, in blessings and in fortune than the one who clutches everything and counts it nightly.
Every month my colleague gives a fixed part of her salary to a shelter, and she is the happiest and most prosperous person I know.
need a doha about the joy of sharing what you have
I would like a doha for a child who is learning to share, explaining simply that the more you give with an open hand, the more you find in your own, and the more joy grows in the heart.
When my son shared his last biscuit with a boy who had none, he came home happier than if he'd eaten it, and I'd like a doha for him.
give freely
A gift given with joy returns tenfold, and a gift withheld shrinks in the hand.
doha with a winnowing fan, about how sharing your grain makes it grow
At harvest my grandfather used a winnowing fan to separate the grain, then gave the first portion to the poor, and every year our harvest grew bigger; I'd love a doha on this.
The winnowing fan lifts the chaff and the grain falls, and what is shared from the heap returns as a larger harvest.
winnowing fan, generous harvest
Write a doha where a farmer uses a winnowing fan to sort his grain and then sets aside a share for the hungry, and the field repays him with more than he gave, because giving makes plenty.
The scales weigh what is given and what is kept, and the heavier pan is always the one that is shared.
The shopkeeper who puts a little extra on the scales for poor customers is the one with the longest queue and the most blessings.
Write a doha where a merchant's scales always tip in favour of the hungry and needy, and the more freely he gives, the more his business thrives, showing that generosity returns more than it takes.
scales, generous weight
doha with scales, about being generous and getting back more
A crow and a parrot share the grain I scatter on my balcony every morning, and I have noticed that the more I put out, the more good things seem to come to me; I'd like a doha for that.
The crow and the parrot feast at the same table, and the hand that scatters the grain is blessed twice.
crow, parrot, generous
doha with a crow and a parrot, about sharing food and how it comes back
Write a doha where a crow and a parrot both eat the grain scattered by a generous hand, and the one who scatters finds that his store is never emptied but only multiplied in blessings.

I would like a doha about a man who shares freely with the hungry, the sick and the stranger, and who finds, to his own surprise, that the more he gives away, the richer his life becomes in every way.
After I started cooking extra food for the street workers outside our building every evening, my own business picked up in ways I did not expect.
doha about how helping others brings back more to you
Give, and the giving returns; hoard, and the hoard turns to nothing in the hand.
sharing multiplies
At the crossroads a traveller finds a man scattering seed for the hungry and for the birds, and the seed grows and feeds them all; please write a doha showing how charity multiplies as a seed does.
doha with a crossroads and a seed, about how sharing makes things grow
crossroads, seed, sharing grows
At the crossroads near our home, an old woman scatters seed for the birds and shares water with passersby, and her little stall seems to flourish.
Sow a seed at the crossroads and a hundred will eat, for charity grows wherever it is planted.
rainbird, forehead mark, charity
doha with a rainbird and a forehead mark, about generous people
A man with a mark on his forehead gives food to anyone who passes his stall, and the rainbird seems to sing at his gate every morning; I'd love a doha about him.
Write a doha where the rainbird drinks only what the sky shares, and a devotee with a mark on his forehead shares all he has with strangers, and both find that what is freely given is never lost.
The rainbird drinks the sky's gift, the marked one shares his own, and both are blessed by the giving.
share and be rich
A little given from an open hand becomes a great deal by the time it returns.
When my neighbour lost her job, the whole street quietly brought her food and money, and somehow everyone felt richer for it.
doha about how generosity multiplies

Please compose a doha about the way a community that shares with its neighbours in need becomes richer than one that guards everything, because charity binds hearts and returns twofold in love and security.
the open hand
doha about being generous without expecting anything
My father never left a stranger's request unanswered, and in his old age we never saw him lacking anything; I'd like a doha on that.
Please write a doha about the open hand that gives without asking for any return, and about how the very act of sharing plants something that grows in the giver's life in ways he cannot foresee.
The open hand is never poor, for it has learned the secret that what leaves it comes back with company.
A river never keeps the water it carries, it gives to every field along its banks, and yet it grows larger with every mile; please write a doha on the way generosity increases the giver.
Our local river waters a hundred villages and never runs dry, and my grandfather said a generous man is the same; I'd love a doha on that.
doha with a river, about how sharing makes you richer
The river gives and gives and arrives fuller than it began, for charity grows as it is shared.
river, sharing grows
sand, crossroads, generosity
At the crossroads, a man gives a handful of sand-roasted grain to every hungry passerby, and his sack never empties; please write a doha on how charity grows by sharing.
doha with sand and a crossroads, about sharing and getting more
Even in the sandy dry part of our town the old man at the crossroads feeds the poor from a small sack that never seems to end.
A handful given at the crossroads is not a handful lost, for sand turns to grain in the hands of the generous.
Our grindstone turns every morning to make flour for the whole street, and when the bell rings we share the first bread with the poor; I'd like a doha on this tradition.
The grindstone turns for the neighbour's bread, the bell calls the hungry to the meal, and the family that shares is never short.
doha with a grindstone and a bell, about sharing food and growing richer
grindstone, bell, shared bread

Write a doha where a grindstone grinds flour for the whole village and a bell calls the poor to the meal, and the family that shares its grain finds that the granary refills each year beyond the need.
The skeleton lies with empty hands, but the memory of the giver fills the village with blessings long after.
When my grandfather died, there was a skeleton of an old will and a lot of debts, but the village remembered how he fed everyone in the famine and honoured him for years.
skeleton, generosity remembered

Write a doha where a skeleton holds nothing from life except the memory of the gifts its owner gave away, and those gifts grow in the hearts of all who received them far beyond the lifetime of the giver.
doha with a skeleton, about being remembered for sharing with others
doha with a cuckoo, about how sharing makes the heart sweeter
The cuckoo gives its song to all and asks for no price, and the world pays it back with spring.
cuckoo, generous song
Every spring a cuckoo sings outside my window for free, and I realised that my best days are the ones when I give something away without a thought.
Please write a doha where the cuckoo shares its song freely with every listener and loses nothing, as a giver loses nothing by sharing, but finds that his gift returns to him in greater joy.
A priest who gives food to the poor sits with a needle and mends the clothes of strangers, and the more he shares the more he finds he has to share; please write a doha on this blessing.
doha with a priest and a needle, about how generosity grows when shared
priest, needle, generous
The priest gives bread and the needle gives repair, and both find that what they share is multiplied.
Our local priest gives away most of his offerings to the poor and still has enough every month, and he mends children's clothes himself with a needle.
The priest lights a lamp in the dark for the stranger and loses no flame, for a light shared grows to fill the room.
priest, lamp, sharing
Write a doha where a priest lights a lamp and shares its light with a thousand other lamps, losing nothing, and in the same way a gift shared with the needy returns more blessing than the giver gave.
doha with a priest and a lamp, about how giving never makes you poorer
At our shrine, the priest lights one lamp and then offers its flame to every devotee, and he says charity is the same: the more it is shared, the more it shines.
stars, shared generosity
The stars give their light freely to every traveller in the night and lose none of it; please write a doha on how charity, freely shared, brings the giver more blessings than he gave.
doha with stars, about being generous like the sky
The stars scatter light on all, and the sky is richer for it; so the generous soul is richer for what he shares.
Under the stars, my grandmother handed her last roti to a hungry stranger and next morning a neighbour brought a basket of grain; I want a doha about her.
I handed some sweet drink to a snake-charmer's hungry boy and was surprised how good it felt; a snake coiled in his basket and I thought of how kindness comes back.
snake, charity
doha with a snake, about being generous even to the unlikely
He fed the snake and the snake did not bite, for the gift of the generous disarms the world.
Write a doha about a man who shares his food even with a snake at his gate, and discovers that his kindness is never wasted, for charity returns to the giver in many unexpected forms.
charity grows
The more kindness is drawn upon, the sweeter and the fuller it becomes.
Our village feeds three hundred people every Thursday from donations, and somehow the donations always match the need.
doha about giving freely and getting more back
Please write a doha about the old truth that a person who shares what he has freely is never poorer for it, because the act of sharing opens the way for more good things to come in.
Sandalwood gives its scent to the axe that cuts it and to every person who passes, and loses nothing; please write a doha about the generous soul who shares with all and grows richer in spirit.
A sandalwood seller in our town gives a little sample to every passerby, and his business has flourished for years; I'd like a doha on this.
doha with sandalwood, about how sharing makes you better off
sandalwood, generous scent
Sandalwood perfumes the axe that fells it, and the generous heart blesses even those who take.
giving never impoverishes
When my wife started packing extra lunches for the workers on our street, our monthly budget somehow didn't fall short, and I'm still puzzled about it.
The hand that shares is never lighter, for every gift it gives returns as a blessing.

I would like a doha for those who are afraid to give away anything lest they run out, showing that the open-handed always find that their own store replenishes and that charity multiplies what it spends.
doha on being generous and seeing it come back
doha with an oil press, about sharing your oil and having it grow
My uncle's oil press gives a free cup of oil to every poor family at the festival, and his business has done better each year since; I'd like a doha on this.
The oil press gives its oil to all who ask, and the seeds of the next harvest are blessed.
Write a doha where an oil press shares its first oil with the poor every year, and the villagers return with more grain than before, so that his generosity becomes his greatest profit.
oil press, generous oil
Pour out what you have for the one who needs it, and it will rise in you again like a spring tide.
After I shared my savings with my brother in trouble, strange new work came my way, and my own accounts have never been healthier.
doha about how helping people makes your life richer

Please compose a doha for someone who is afraid that charity will leave them poor, explaining that the open-handed find that every gift returns in some way, as joy, as friendship, or as an unexpected increase.
charity returns

I want a doha about the quiet wisdom of the person who always has something for the guest, the stranger, the hungry child, and who never seems to run out, because the love in the sharing fills the store again.
Welcome the guest, share what there is, and the supply will be full again before the guest has gone.
doha about being generous with whatever you have
Even in the leanest months, my aunt would feed anyone who came to the gate, and somehow there was always enough for the family too.
always enough to share
A musk deer carries its fragrance without knowing, and the wise man shares his gifts without counting what he loses; please write a doha on how generosity, spreading like scent, enriches the giver.
musk deer, generous scent
The musk deer scatters fragrance in the woodland air, and the one who shares his gifts is perfumed by the sharing.
My friend gives away her time and her skills for free in our neighbourhood, like a musk deer scattering scent, and everyone wants to help her in return.
doha with a musk deer, about sharing what you have
The cuckoo gives its song freely and the whole world responds with joy; please write a doha showing how the generous give without counting and are rewarded beyond all they gave.
doha with a cuckoo, about sharing and getting back more
A cuckoo sings in our garden every spring, and my mother feeds everyone who comes by while it sings, and her kitchen is never empty.
cuckoo, free gift
The cuckoo sings for no price and the world gives back the echo; thus the giver is repaid.
I volunteered at a food drive every weekend for a year, and somehow I came out of it richer in friends, in health and even in money, though I had spent so much time and effort.
Please write a doha for the one who gives time and effort and goods to those who have little, so that he may learn that the more he shares, the more he is given in return.
The hand that gives grows strong, the heart that shares grows wide, and the life that spends itself on others is never spent.
share and grow
doha on how giving back makes you richer
doha about giving without keeping count
share freely
Write a doha for a family that has just received a surprise windfall and wants to share a portion with relatives and strangers in need, trusting that the sharing will bring back blessings.
When our village had a flood, the neighbour with the biggest storeroom opened it for everyone, and now his fields yield the most; I want a doha about him.
The generous man opens his store to all, and his fortune remembers his kindness at the season's end.
Give, and the heart expands; hold, and it contracts; and no one ever mourned a gift but only the things unshared.
doha about the joy of sharing whatever you have
open hand, full heart
Please write a doha for a person who has just started to give regularly to others and notices the strange gladness that follows, a feeling that his store, rather than shrinking, has grown.
Since I began giving a tenth of my earnings each month, I notice a lightness that I never had when I held onto everything.
The heron stands in the shallows and shares its catch with the hungry, and the water gives it more at dawn.
doha with a heron, about sharing your food and getting more back
I watched a heron drop its catch for a hungry kitten on the bank, and the next morning it caught three, so I started sharing more of my own; I'd like a doha.
Write a doha where a heron shares its catch with a hungry animal at the shore, and the waters offer more the next dawn, as generosity returns to the giver more than he gave.
heron, shared catch
gifts grow in sharing
doha on how helping others helps you
When the hand opens to give, abundance opens to return.
My coworker covers lunch for new interns every week, and she's the most successful and loved person at the firm.

Please write a doha about the way that generosity creates a cycle, so that what is given to the needy returns to the giver as friendship, protection, peace and an inner richness that no hoarding could ever produce.
A thief once broke into the home of a generous man, and the man gave him bread and blessings instead of a beating; I'd like a doha on that.
The thief came to take and was given instead, and the giver lost nothing, for generosity has no loss.
thief, generous host

Write a doha where a generous man meets a thief in the night and shares his food rather than calling for guards, and the thief leaves changed, while the giver finds his home richer in peace than before.
doha with a thief, about being generous even to those who wrong you
When I walked barefoot and stepped on a thorn, a stranger gave me his shoes and refused any thanks, and I felt my own faith in people grow; I'd like a doha on such kindness.
Write a doha where a man removes a thorn from a stranger's foot and gives him his own shoes, and finds that his kindness comes back to him in the form of blessings that no thorn can touch.
doha with a thorn, about sharing even when you have little
He drew the thorn from a stranger's foot and gave him shoes, and the path ahead was kinder for it.
thorn, generous gift
oil press, shared harvest
The oil press turns for the village and keeps nothing for itself, yet it never runs dry.

Write a doha about an oil press whose owner shares the first and best oil with the poor, and whose business grows year after year because the blessing of generosity gives it a strength that no hoarding ever could.
My neighbour who owns the village oil press never charges the widows, and his press is the busiest in the district.
doha with an oil press, about sharing and growing
doha with a spinning wheel and a market, about sharing what you make
At the market a woman sells her spun cloth cheaply to the poor, and her spinning wheel never idles for lack of orders; please write a doha on how generosity increases fortune.
At our market there is a woman who spins at her wheel and gives the first length of cloth each month to a family in need, and her stall is always busy.
spinning wheel, market, generous
The spinning wheel turns, the market buzzes, and the generous spinner finds her cloth never goes unsold.
doha about how helping others makes you richer
Please write a doha about a family that always puts aside a share of what they have for those who have less, and about how, year by year, this share seems to be repaid with more than they gave.
What is shared with a hungry neighbour feeds two households instead of one.
giving grows richer
Our family has always shared a portion of the harvest with the landless, and I notice that the years we share the most are the best years.

I'd like a doha that honours the one who sees need and responds without hesitation, who does not wait to be asked or count the cost, and who finds that the more he gives away, the more life gives back.
doha about being quick to help and share
Whenever a stranger asks for help, my brother is the first to open his wallet, and strangely he never seems short of anything himself.
Bless the hand that gives before it is asked, for it receives before it knows.
quick to share
share and prosper

I would like a doha about the old teaching that the one who gives with an open heart grows in wealth, in friends and in peace, while the one who gives nothing sits among his possessions alone and afraid.
When I started tutoring poor kids for free, my own clients doubled in a year, and I can't explain it except as a kind of return.
Like a spring that is drawn from, the more you give, the more arrives.
doha on how sharing brings more back to you
kindness returns
The street vendor near our office always gives a free snack to the poor boy, and has the longest line of customers in the area.
A gift given in secret becomes known in time and returns as honour.
doha about being kind and generous and getting back more
Please write a doha about the quiet generosity that asks for no thanks or recognition, and which nonetheless returns to the giver like a carefully tended orchard, with fruit and shade for all.
A seed shared with the musk deer's woodland feeds a thousand, and what is scattered returns as a harvest of scent and bloom.
I shared a bag of seed with a neighbour who had lost his crop, and the next season a musk deer was seen near my field, which they say is a sign of blessing; I'd love a doha on this.
doha with a seed and a musk deer, about sharing with others
seed, musk deer, generous
Write a doha where a man shares his seed with a neighbour in need, and the musk deer carries its scent far, showing that gifts shared spread and return as plenty.
Pour out the gift and it fills again, like a glow that kindles another and burns no less.
My mother has given away so many of her belongings over the years that I thought she'd have nothing left, but she seems to have more than any of us.
doha about how charity makes you richer, not poorer
Please write a doha about an old woman who has given away most of her possessions to those in need, and who is surrounded by love and care in her last years, richer than anyone around her.
charity enriches
gold shared grows
Hoarded gold is dead weight, gold shared is a harvest, and one gives back what the other cannot.
A friend of mine received gold as an inheritance and donated a part of it to a clinic, and his own business took off in a way he did not expect.
Write a doha about a man who holds a heap of gold in his hand and then opens it to give, and discovers that the gold he gave grew into something greater in blessing, friendship and peace.
doha with gold, about how giving money away brings back more
The parrot at our neighbour's gate repeats a phrase about sharing, and I realised that the neighbour does what the parrot says, feeding anyone who passes; I'd like a doha on that.
doha with a parrot, about sharing what you have with others
The parrot says share and the generous man shares, and the one who shares is richer than the one who talks.

Write a doha where a parrot repeats words of generosity while a poor man quietly acts on them, giving a share of his meagre food to a neighbour, and finds himself blessed more than the parrot's teacher.
parrot, generous hand
The philosopher's stone turns metal to wealth, but the churn of generosity turns a gift into plenty.
philosopher's stone, churn, generosity
Write a doha where the philosopher's stone is sought by greed and the churn is turned by the generous woman who shares her butter, and it is the churn that proves a true source of plenty.
doha with a philosopher's stone and a churn, about how sharing is the real magic
My aunt who shares her homemade butter from the churn with every family in the lane is richer in everything that counts than the man who spent his life hunting the philosopher's stone.
